title: Matchings are no larger than coverings
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. If $M$ is a matching in $G$ and $K$ is a covering of $G$, then the number of edges of $M$ is at most the number of vertices in $K$; that is, $\abs{M} \le \abs{K}$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
M is a matching in G
K is a covering of G
replaced:
(5.5): for any matching \texttt{M} and covering \texttt{K}, \texttt{|M| $\le$ |K|}.

If $K$ is a covering of $G$, and $M$ is a matching of $G$, then $K$ contains at least
one end of each of the edges in $M$. Thus, for any matching $M$ and any covering $K$,
$|M| \le |K|$. Indeed, if $M^*$ is a maximum matching and $\tilde{K}$ is a minimum
covering, then \[|M^*| \le |\tilde{K}| \qquad (5.5)\]

The book states this inline, without a theorem number or separate proof.
